Each voxel stores a single floating-point value representing the truncated signed distance [S2].

The claim states that each voxel stores a single floating-point value representing the truncated signed distance. Source [S2] defines the Truncated Signed Distance Field (TSDF) as a function $d(p)$ that maps a point in 3D space to a value within a specific interval $[d_{min}, d_{max}]$. The notes and passages confirm that TSDF values are computed using a signed distance formula ($I_{±}(p) ||p - q||_2$) and then truncated. Since the text describes a 'voxel-based representation' where these values are stored and processed (e.g., 'sub-volumes sampled... at every eight voxels'), and the TSDF value is a single scalar result of the defined function, the evidence supports that each voxel stores this single floating-point value.

For each voxel center $p$ in the $W \times H \times D$ grid, find the closest point $q$ on the surface $Q$ [S2].

The claim states that for each voxel center $p$, the closest point $q$ on the surface $Q$ is found. Source [S2] explicitly defines the TSDF value $d(p)$ using the term $I_{+}(p) = sign(n(q)^T (p - q))$, where $q$ is defined as the point on the surface $Q$ that minimizes the distance $||p - q||_2$ (i.e., the closest point). The formula $d(p) = min(d_{max}, max(d_{min}, I_{+}(p) min_{q in Q} ||p - q||_2))$ confirms that the calculation relies on identifying this closest point $q$ for every point $p$ (including voxel centers in the grid). Therefore, the evidence supports the claim that finding the closest point $q$ is part of the process described.
